result.summary:
Flipped docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-035 status from pending to done (no content correction needed -- RELEASE-VALIDATOR's independent re-verification of all 10 ACs matches the requirement's description/AC text exactly). Appended one 'done' event to docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (at 2026-09-08T09:47:24Z, real clock time) summarizing RELEASE-VALIDATOR's independent re-verification: lint/build clean, full vitest suite 358/358 twice, AC5 concurrency file 7/7 clean runs total, all 10 ACs individually re-checked against actual shipped code, scope discipline clean (zero diff on checkinQr.ts, zero schema/migration change). git diff --numstat confirmed 0 deletions on both edited files before committing.

CONCLUSION ON THE 'STARTED EVENT' QUESTION: RELEASE-VALIDATOR's finding is a REAL gap, not a misunderstanding of convention -- but it is a pre-existing, recurring gap, not something unique to REQ-035. WF-02_requirement_implementation.md's Step 00 explicitly documents 'On PASS: ORCH flips status to in_progress ... and appends a started event' as the intended procedure. Checking actual precedent in docs/status/requirement_status.yaml: REQ-033 DID get a proper 'started' event at Step 00 (2026-09-08T00:00:00Z) before its 'done' event -- so the two-event pattern is the documented and sometimes-followed convention, not itself a misunderstanding. However REQ-034's history shows the IDENTICAL gap RELEASE-VALIDATOR flagged for REQ-035: only a 'done' event exists for REQ-034, going pending -> done directly with no started event ever recorded, and no note flagged it as a gap at the time. So the finding is correct that a started event is supposed to exist and didn't for REQ-035, but it is the SECOND consecutive time (REQ-034, now REQ-035) this has happened in Release 2, meaning Step 00's actual execution (not its written procedure) has been silently skipping this consistently for two runs running -- not a one-off slip and not a misreading of the convention.

No backdated 'started' event was fabricated for REQ-035: core-directives.md's bookkeeping rules require timestamps to come from the clock, never be estimated, and there is no way to recover the real Step 00 start time accurately now. This matches the choice implicitly already made when REQ-034 was closed with no backfill attempt. requirements.yaml's status was flipped directly pending -> done (there was no real in_progress window to represent). The gap is documented in the done event's note itself so it is visible in the audit trail rather than silently smoothed over, and is reported below as a recurring MINOR issue for ORCH, since this is now a pattern across 2 of the last 3 Release 2 runs, not a single incident DOC-UPDATER can close by editing history.

Recommend ORCH verify why (e.g. Step 00 handoffs for Release 2 have been produced by FRONTEND-DEV without ORCH's own follow-up status-file edit landing in the same commit) and correct the actual practice going forward -- no history was rewritten to fix past runs, per append-only rules.
